text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A rival faction within the biggest Independent Trade Union will hold a convention to coincide with the main trade union meeting.
- The head of a company in the northern city of Shkoder has disappeared with $13 million leaving 30,000 Albanians who had put their money in his pyramid scheme.
- Frictions continue in the opposition Socialist party.
- President Sali Berisha has denounced former Albanian King Ahmet Zog for abandoning the country in 1939 when Italian troops occupied it.
- Albanian parliament on Thursday passed a law on setting up a committee to investigate the Balkan country's 'get-rich-quick' pyramid schemes.
- Miners claim the privatisation of their industry is open to corruption and have asked the government to make the privatisation method public.
- Tritan Shehu, leader of the Democratic Party, deputy prime minister and foreign minister, suffered a slight health problem.
- The vaccine immunisation campaign has been effective against the polio outbreak in Albania, a doctor at the hospital for infectious diseases said.
- Bad weather in the northern district of Lezhe has disrupted normal life. Schools have been temporarily closed in some villages because of lack of power.
- Bad weather swept Albania in the last days killing one old man in the eastern town of Librazhd. Wind gusted up to 110 km per hour in the western city of Durres.
- Parliament created a commission on Albania's "European integration" which is one of the post-communist country's main goals.
- A small civil airport was re-opened in the northern city of Shkoder.
- The privatisation process of Albania's state-owned banks will start within this year.
